issues.description: The problem specification (and UML) expects a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) on SealSaloon, but the solution implementation provides a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int) instead. This name/signature mismatch is structural: students following the specification will implement or call acceptSupplyDelivery, while the provided solution (and potentially tests) uses a different method name, causing confusion or failing integrations.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method receiveDelivery to acceptSupplyDelivery to match the problem specification and UML, or add a new static acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) method that delegates to receiveDelivery. Ensure the method name in the solution, template (if provided), and tests match the name used in the problem statement.

issues.description: The problem statement and the provided Main use a method named acceptSupplyDelivery(...) to register incoming stock deliveries, but the solution's SealSaloon class implements this functionality under a different identifier receiveDelivery(...). This naming mismatch across artifacts (problem statement, template/solution Main, and SealSaloon) breaks the direct mapping students must make between the requirement and the implementation and can lead to confusion or failing calls/tests expecting acceptSupplyDelivery.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method receiveDelivery to acceptSupplyDelivery and keep the same signature (public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)). Update any calls (e.g., in Main) to use acceptSupplyDelivery so names are consistent with the problem statement and UML.
